title: E0074: Weak random number generator
plain_english: Generating security-sensitive values (such as tokens, keys, salts, or CSRF tokens) with `rand()` or `mt_rand()` is unsafe because these functions are not cryptographically secure.
why_matters: `rand()` and `mt_rand()` use weak pseudorandom number generators. Attackers may be able to: - Predict future random values from prior outputs - Guess session tokens, CSRF tokens, or password reset tokens - Bypass authentication or authorization
good_example:
$token = bin2hex(random_bytes(16));  // cryptographically secure
$key = random_int(1000, 9999);       // cryptographically secure
what_it_checks: `rand()`, `mt_rand()`, and `uniqid()` used for security-sensitive purposes (tokens, keys, salts)
`mt_rand()` without seeding from a secure source
